text:
Boring Money Monday.

You only need three numbers to start: what comes in each month, what goes out, and how many months you could keep going if nothing changed.

Not a budget. Not a plan. Just three numbers on one page.

Grab the free Three Numbers Starter Sheet at the link in bio.

Day one counts.

Here is the whole first step of getting your money together:

Write down what came in last month. Write down what went out. Then see how many months what you have could cover.

That last number does not have to be big. It just has to be known.

The free Starter Sheet is at the link in bio.

Day one counts.

If the word budget makes your shoulders go up, skip it.

Start with one question: what actually came in last month? Check your bank app. Say the number out loud.

That is not a judgment. It is a starting point.

The free Three Numbers Starter Sheet is at the link in bio.

Day one counts.

Boring Money Monday, the short version.

In: what arrives.
Out: what leaves.
Months: how long you could keep going.

Fill those in once a month and you will know where you stand.

The free one-page Starter Sheet is at the link in bio.

Day one counts.

Before you cut anything, decide what is worth keeping.

That is the Worth-It Rule: protect what is worth it first, then look at the rest.

What is one thing on your keep list this month? Tell me below, no judgment.

Day one counts.

You are allowed to keep things that make life feel livable.

A cutting spree that leaves you miserable is hard to stick with. Choose a few things on purpose and keep them without guilt.

What is something small you refuse to give up?

Day one counts.

Try this in ten minutes: write down five things you spend money on that you would be sad to lose.

Circle the two that matter most. Those go on the keep list.

Which two would you circle?

Day one counts.

Keeping something is a decision, not a failure.

If a small expense holds your week together, name it and stop apologizing for it.

Follow along for one small money step a day, and tell me what is on your keep list.

Day one counts.

Quiet leaks are the easy first cut.

Open your bank app, scroll back one month, and circle any charge you do not recognize or no longer use. No shame, just circle.

Part 2 of the $17 Day Zero Workbook, Where It Went, walks you through it. Link in bio.

Day one counts.

Dreading a phone call to cancel something or ask for a lower bill?

You are not alone. The Dreaded Call Scripts in the $17 Day Zero Workbook give you words to read, so you do not have to find them in the moment.

Link in bio.

Day one counts.

Autopay is great until you forget what is on it.

Twenty minutes, one list of every bill that pulls money automatically. That is the whole task.

The Year-at-a-Glance Bill Tracker in the $17 Day Zero Workbook gives you a place to keep it. Link in bio.

Day one counts.

You do not have to cut everything. You have to look.

Keep, Cut, Earn, Build is the order, and Cut comes second on purpose. Protect what is worth it first.

It is all in the 32-page Day Zero Workbook, $17. Link in bio.

Day one counts.

Earning more does not have to mean a new career.

Write down three things people already ask you for help with. That list is where small earning ideas start. No promises about amounts, just ideas.

What do people always ask you for help with?

Day one counts.

One question for today: what could you do with a phone or a laptop that someone would pay a fair price for?

You do not need the whole answer. Write one idea down.

Drop yours below. Follow along for one small money step a day.

Day one counts.

Before you add a side income, check what it would cost you in time.

Five hours a week is five hours you have to find. Look at your calendar first.

A small idea that fits your life beats a big one that does not.

What would you say no to, to make room?

Day one counts.

Skills you already have count.

Writing, organizing, teaching, fixing things, staying calm in a crisis. Make a list of ten and do not edit it.

What is the first skill on your list?

Day one counts.

A first-hour setup for your money:

List every account you have. Write down every bill and its due date. Change the passwords you reuse.

None of it is glamorous. All of it is a foundation.

Part 4 of the $17 Day Zero Workbook, The First Hour, walks you through it. Link in bio.

Day one counts.

No time for a big project? Try the Fifteen-Minute Start.

It is one of the bonuses in the $17 Day Zero Workbook, for the days when you can only do one small thing.

Small counts. Link in bio.

Day one counts.

Build slowly. Fast and perfect is not the goal.

This week: one account list. Next week: one bill calendar. After that: one small cushion.

The 32-page Day Zero Workbook, $17, lays out the order. Link in bio.

Day one counts.

Questions for a Money Helper is a bonus page in the $17 Day Zero Workbook.

Before you meet with anyone about money, it helps to know what to ask.

A licensed professional can help with the big decisions. This helps you walk in prepared. Link in bio.

Day one counts.

If you are doing the money math at 2 A.M., you are not failing. You are scared, and that is human.

Write the numbers down and close the notebook. Look at them in daylight. They often feel smaller on paper.

Who else has done the 2 A.M. math?

Day one counts.

Ask where did the money go, not why did I let this happen.

Where is a question with an answer. Why is a trap.

Open one statement and just answer where. Save this for the next time the why voice shows up.

Day one counts.

You do not have to feel ready.

Starting over with money is clumsy at first. Give yourself a slow week. One small task. Then rest.

Zero is a starting line. Follow along, and we will keep the steps small.

Day one counts.

Permission slip for this weekend:

You may go slowly. You may be bad at this at first. You may need to read the same page twice.

Send this to a friend who needs it.

Day one counts.

The Monthly Twenty: twenty calm minutes, once a month.

Look at your three numbers again. Did anything change? Pick one small step for next month.

The free Three Numbers Starter Sheet is a good place to write them. Link in bio.

Day one counts.

Sunday reset, small version:

Open your bank app. Check what came in and what went out this week. Write down one number you want to remember.

Ten minutes, then close it. The free Starter Sheet is at the link in bio.

Day one counts.

Once a month, ask three questions.

What came in? What went out? How many months could I keep going?

Get the free Three Numbers Starter Sheet at the link in bio and write your answers on one page.

Day one counts.

Put the Monthly Twenty on your calendar like an appointment with a friend.

Same day every month. Same short list. What gets looked at gets easier.

The free Starter Sheet is at the link in bio.

Day one counts.
